sentences.text:
This petition has been filed under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (in short,
'Cr.P.C.') seeking quashing of FIR No.0171/2019 registered at Police Station: Gokulpuri, North-East District, under Sections 498A/406/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (in short, 'IPC'), along with all other proceedings arising therefrom, on the basis of a settlement.
sentences._hearing_file: Chander Shekhar And Ors vs State & Anr on 16 February, 2024.json

sentences.text:
2. The learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the petitioner no.1 and respondent no.2 got married on 09.02.2018, as per Hindu rites and customs and the subject FIR was an offshoot of the matrimonial discord between the parties, that is, the petitioner no.1 and the respondent no.2.

Pursuant to the above Settlement between the parties, the learned Family Court has granted Divorce to the petitioner no. 1 and the respondent no. 2 by mutual consent vide Decree of Divorce dated 28.03.2022.
5.
sentences._hearing_file: Chander Shekhar And Ors vs State & Anr on 16 February, 2024.json

sentences.text:
The present petition complained that the respondent no.2 was not cooperating in quashing of the present FIR, which is in violation of the terms of the settlement entered into between the parties,
and the petitioner no.1 has also filed a petition for initiating action under the Contempt of Courts Act against her, being CONT.CAS(C) No. 940/2022, titled as Chander Shekhar v. Laxmi Devi, which is pending adjudication.
sentences._hearing_file: Chander Shekhar And Ors vs State & Anr on 16 February, 2024.json

sentences.text: 6. The respondent no.2, who is present in Court in person and has been duly identified by the Investigating Officer (IO), reaffirms the settlement and states that she has settled all the inter se disputes with the petitioners of her own free will and without any coercion.
sentences._hearing_file: Chander Shekhar And Ors vs State & Anr on 16 February, 2024.json

sentences.text: The respondent no.2 submits that she does not wish to pursue the proceedings emanating from the FIR any further and has no objection if the present FIR is quashed.
sentences._hearing_file: Chander Shekhar And Ors vs State & Anr on 16 February, 2024.json

sentences.text: 7. The petitioner no.1, who is also present in person in court, submits that he would not press his Contempt Petition any further and would be withdrawing the same.
sentences._hearing_file: Chander Shekhar And Ors vs State & Anr on 16 February, 2024.json

sentences.text: 8. I have perused the contents of the FIR and also the settlement This is a digitally signed order.

sentences.text:
As the disputes between the parties arose out of a matrimonial relationship,
and now the same have been amicably settled, a decree of divorce has also been passed by the learned Family Court pursuant to the settlement, and also looking into the nature of the allegations made in the complaint, and binding the petitioner no.1 to the statement made hereinabove, in my opinion, no useful purpose would be served in keeping the FIR alive.
sentences._hearing_file: Chander Shekhar And Ors vs State & Anr on 16 February, 2024.json

sentences.text: In fact, it would rather create further acrimony between the parties and will be an unnecessary burden on the State exchequer.
sentences._hearing_file: Chander Shekhar And Ors vs State & Anr on 16 February, 2024.json

sentences.text: 10. Guided by the principles enunciated by the Supreme Court in its judgments in Jitendra Raghuvanshi v. Babita Raghuvanshi, (2013) 4 SCC 58, Gian Singh v. State of Punjab, (2012) 10 SCC 303; Parbatbhai Aahir @ Parbatbhai Bhimsinbhai Karmur & Ors. v. State of Gujarat & Ors., (2017) 9 SCC 641; and, State of Haryana & Ors. v. Bhajan Lal & Ors., 1992 Supp (1) SCC 3, this Court deems it appropriate, in the interest of justice, to exercise its inherent powers under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C. to quash the FIR and all the proceedings emanating therefrom.
